title: Second-round editing command responsiveness improvements
scope: Invocation-local command/selection work after editor activation. Startup, loading and pre-existing implementation register improvements excluded.
validation: Focused operation-count and behavior fixtures plus existing rendered envelope, take graph, frame-canonical transform and v21 preservation tests. These are Node work measurements, not Electron end-to-end latency or FPS.

findings.change: Replace complete-document rescans per relationship-chain hop with one traversal of each group and A/V link.

test.name: relationship chains visit each relationship a bounded number of times and preserve project order

findings.evidence: 600 alternating-chain clips: 1439400 relationship reads before, 2400 after.
findings.limitations: Work-count measured; each invocation still builds its local graph.

findings.change: Pass the existing availableClips map into relationship expansion instead of indexing every clip twice.

test.name: selection ownership traverses each track membership once per resolution

findings.evidence: One availability map per authority resolution; same graph helper consumes it.
findings.limitations: Code-confirmed removed map build; no isolated wall-time attribution.

findings.change: Build first-owner membership lookup once instead of searching track clipIds for every selected clip.

test.name: selection ownership traverses each track membership once per resolution

findings.evidence: 250 clips in 250 tracks: 31375 membership reads before, 250 after.
findings.limitations: Work-count measured; membership table construction remains linear.

findings.change: Resolve every selected clip owner through one membership table instead of a track search per clip.

test.name: selection ownership traverses each track membership once per resolution

findings.evidence: Full selection resolution uses at most three reads per track; preserves missing-owner refusal.
findings.limitations: Its own invocation-local table is rebuilt, preserving mutable caller semantics.

findings.change: Resolve clip IDs once before sorting rather than performing two linear project searches per comparison.

test.name: sorting decorates geometry once and keeps deterministic code-unit ties

findings.evidence: 1000 reversed clips: 999999 identity reads before, 1000 after. A two-clip early track visits only its two records, avoiding a scan of the unrelated 10000-clip tail.
findings.limitations: Work-count measured; standalone lookup stops after all requested IDs are found; sort still performs O(k log k) numeric comparisons.

findings.change: Capture each participating clip start and stable tie ID once, eliminating repeated clip property reads in comparisons.

findings.limitations: Code-confirmed repeated property reads removed; combined sort count includes identity indexing.

findings.evidence: Range-only selection: four project collection reads before, zero after.
findings.limitations: Explicit identity arrays still trigger their necessary membership index.

test.name: rendered replacement resolves independent components without repeatedly scanning unrelated identities

findings.evidence: Only affectedTracks feed sortTrack; unrelated memberships and clip objects are preserved.
findings.limitations: Touched tracks sort; untouched authored membership order is retained even if unsorted. Duplicate IDs/owners use legacy whole-project traversal/sorting. Full persisted validation remains authoritative; direct helpers do not validate unrelated memberships.

helperCompatibility: Persisted commands validate the complete incoming and resulting project. Direct mutable helpers check affected indexed memberships and preserve ReferenceError refusal; unrelated malformed memberships are not scanned for repair. Duplicate clip IDs retain last-match relationship expansion and first-match replacement, while duplicate track IDs/owners use legacy traversal. On valid documents, untouched membership arrays keep their authored order, including unsorted order; only touched tracks are sorted. This intentional preservation differs from the former incidental whole-project sorting.
